## Pull request overview

Adds protocol-layer constants and storage-name mapping utilities to decouple system object/field identifiers from physical table/column names, supporting flexible DB schemas while keeping the protocol stable.

**Changes:**
- Introduces `SystemObjectName` / `SystemFieldName` protocol constants and exports them from `@objectstack/spec/system`.
- Adds optional `columnName` to `FieldSchema` to allow per-field physical column overrides (complementing existing `ObjectSchema.tableName`).
- Adds `StorageNameMapping` helpers and tests, and updates the roadmap to reflect completed storage-name mapping support.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 8 out of 8 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

<details>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/spec/src/system/index.ts | Re-exports system constants from the system protocol entrypoint. |
| packages/spec/src/system/constants/index.ts | Exports the new system name constants module. |
| packages/spec/src/system/constants/system-names.ts | Adds `SystemObjectName`, `SystemFieldName`, and `StorageNameMapping` utilities. |
| packages/spec/src/system/constants/system-names.test.ts | Adds unit tests covering constants and mapping utilities. |
| packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts | Adds `columnName?: string` to `FieldSchema` for physical column mapping. |
| packages/spec/src/data/field.test.ts | Adds tests asserting `columnName` parsing behavior. |
| packages/spec/src/data/object.test.ts | Adds a test verifying `tableName` + `columnName` are accepted together. |
| ROADMAP.md | Marks storage-name mapping/constants work as completed in Phase 1 deliverables. |
</details>

This file introduces runtime utility functions (`StorageNameMapping`), but `system/constants/index.ts` documents the constants module with “Strict Types, No Logic” / “NO runtime business logic”. To avoid confusing consumers, either move `StorageNameMapping` into a `utils` module (outside `constants`) or update the constants-module docs to explicitly allow pure, stateless helpers like this.
